video_title: Can A 35 Year Old Kawhi REALLY Win Again In Toronto? | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Raptors pay a steep price to acquire Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: The Raptors they paid a pretty steep price. They give up Brandon Ingram, they give up Gradey Dick
quotes.quote: The Raptors they paid a pretty steep price. They give up Brandon Ingram, they give up Gradey Dick, who was a first-round draft pick very recently. They give up two first-round picks, they give up a swap. So they are paying a premium to get a mid-30s Kawhi Leonard who they are now going to turn around and give a contract extension to.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Raptors were better off trading assets for Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: They were better off trading our quote-unquote future of what was Gradey Dick and Brandon Ingram
quotes.quote: At their very best, if they were looking if Kawhi was there last year, maybe they say they make it to the second round. Maybe you scream out you can argue Eastern Conference Finals. But I think at very least they are probably just sitting there being like, we are better off trading you know our quote-unquote future of what was Gradey Dick and so on and so forth and trying to rebuild and Brandon Ingram for the last few years of what Kawhi could be.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Raptors front office shows aggression in pursuing Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: I give the Raptors front office a lot of credit for their aggressiveness.
quotes.quote: I give the Raptors front office a lot of credit for their aggressiveness. It is the same basic front office that was there in 2018. Bobby Webster is now running the show instead of Masai Ujiri, so you have the same a lot of the same people there. They know Kawhi, they believe in Kawhi, they trust Kawhi. Obviously Kawhi is going into this situation with a little bit more of a different mindset. He is very open to an extension with this team, so I would expect him to be there for multiple years.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Raptors face a tough challenge to become true contenders
quotes.excerpt: Defensively they would have to very much come together and turn it into a chess match.
quotes.quote: I don't see that. Even when you said Philadelphia, I believe in Kawhi, but that would be a tough task. That would be a tall order. I mean defensively they would have to very much come together and turn it into a chess match. Now you go from could Emmanuel Quickley be good enough to match up versus Maxey? Could Scotty Barnes lock down LeBron James? And then RJ Barrett can you know can test with Jaylen Brown. Even though I mean I get I would guess Kawhi will guard LeBron James, but even then you don't have a matchup for Joel Embiid in the next three.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's playmaking can elevate Raptors' supporting cast
quotes.excerpt: I think he can take some of the playmaking responsibilities away from an Emmanuel Quickley or an RJ Barrett
quotes.quote: I think he can take some of the playmaking responsibilities away from an Emmanuel Quickley or an RJ Barrett who I don't think are they are not great playmakers. They have strengths, but they are not great playmakers. I think having Kawhi there helps them I think significantly. I think the development of Murray is going to be big too. I like Murray better as the five in Toronto than Jakob Poeltl honestly. Poeltl is not much of a rim protector and I like Murray, he is undersized for that position, but he can get after it, rebound the ball and I think they are better with that kind of small lineup.
